qbXML: `CustomerQueryRq`.

Finds customers and jobs: exact ones by `list_id` or `full_name`, or a filtered set by name, `active_status` and modified date. Without `active_status` only active customers come back. Set `iterator` to page through a long list: each page arrives at your `webhook_url` under one request id.

Important: We highly recommend that you use the `include` tag in your CustomerQuery to include any data you want but do NOT include the `ship_address` data in the Response, unless you need to get the shipping address for a particular customer. Excluding the shipping address data will significantly improve the performance of the CustomerQuery.

Intuit's reference: [CustomerQuery](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/customerquery).

qbXML: `DataExtModRq`, from qbXML 2.0. The `data_ext_mod` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

This request can only be invoked if a data extension definition has already been added to the target object (for example, the customer John Henry) by a DataExtDefAdd or by the user specifying a custom field value for that object via the QuickBooks UI.

If you want to clear the data extension value (to make the custom field or private extension blank), you must use DataExtDel. The DataExtMod request can’t be used to clear the field.

Both DataExtAdd and DataExtMod cause a Modify event to be generated for the parent object. For example invoking one of these on a Customer causes a Customer Modify event. The Time Modified value for that parent object is also updated.

Notice that the Mod operation doesn’t support macros like DataExtAdd does.

Intuit's reference: [DataExtMod](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/dataextmod).

qbXML: `InvoiceAddRq`. The `invoice_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Adds an invoice: what a customer owes for a sale they didn't pay in full when it was made (a sale paid in full is a sales receipt). `customer_ref` is required. Each line in `invoice_line_add` names an `item_ref` and two of `quantity`, `rate` and `amount`; QuickBooks works out the third. An inventory item on an invoice lowers stock and posts its cost of goods sold. To invoice a sales order, link it with `link_to_txn_id`. The `create_invoice` workflow template adds the customer and any missing items first.

In QuickBooks, invoices and estimates use similar fields, and an estimate can be converted into an invoice after the customer accepts the estimate. However, in the SDK, there is currently no ability to create an invoice directly from an estimate (you can’t link an invoice to an estimate).

If you Add an invoice that has an inventory item on it, QB will automatically calculate COGS and post it to the COGS account. (The inventory item will need to be setup to post to the COGS account and must have a unit cost in it.) However, notice that such an InvoiceAdd has sales prices, not cost, so the Add isn’t impacting the cost of the item. The cost of the item is only affected by purchases (bills and item receipts) sales and inventory adjustments.

See also: [Inventory costing](https://docs.qubesync.com/quickbooks-notes#inventory-costing), [Line item taxes](https://docs.qubesync.com/quickbooks-notes#line-item-taxes).

In QuickBooks, most transactions can be categorized either by account or by type (invoice, check, and so on). post.description:
qbXML: `VehicleMileageAddRq`, from qbXML 6.0. The `vehicle_mileage_add` wrapper from qbXML is also accepted.

Adds a VehicleMileage transaction involving the specified vehicle for the specified total miles or optionally for the QuickBooks calculated total miles if you supply the odometer start and end.

Notice that only dates are supported for vehicle mileage, so make sure you enter any datetime values with dates only, no time values. That is, 2002-02-02 will work for trip end date or start date, but 2002-02-02T12:20:20 won’t work.

The mileage contained in this transaction is multiplied by the standard mileage rate allowed by the tax authority and entered by the QuickBooks user in the Enter Vehicle Mileage form. If you’re curious to see what this rate currently is, and the allowable tax expense resulting from this transaction, those are contained in the `standard_mileage_rate` and `standard_mileage_total_amount` fields in the response to this request. The Mileage By Vehicle detail and summary reports track this vehicle expense.

The customer, item, class reference fields are mainly used if a customer is to be charged for mileage, in which case the `billable_status` is set to Billable. In this usage, customer and item references are required, class is optional. The mileage transaction will consequently appear as an outstanding billable time and cost charge for the customer when you create an invoice for that customer. (If class tracking is turned on in QuickBooks, and you supply a class in this transaction, the class will automatically appear in the invoice.) This aspect of the mileage transaction is tracked in the Mileage By Job detail and summary reports.

Important: currently, only the QuickBooks user can put these outstanding charges in the invoice. The SDK doesn’t support this.

If you specify HasBeenBilled in the `billable_status` field, the transaction shows up as Billed in the Mileage By Job reports, but not on the list of outstanding billable customer time and cost charges when an invoice is created.

Intuit's reference: [VehicleMileageAdd](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbdesktop/docs/api-reference/qbdesktop/vehiclemileageadd).
